items.title: FDA clears Elucid FFR-IQ: AI FFR-CT software that adds plaque composition to coronary physiology estimates
items.summary: On October 21, 2026, Elucid announced FDA 510(k) clearance of FFR-IQ, AI software that estimates fractional flow reserve noninvasively from coronary CT angiography by combining coronary anatomy with plaque composition.
bullets: **Elucid FFR-IQ** received **FDA 510(k) clearance** (letter dated **29 Sep 2026**, announced **21 Oct**): AI software estimating **FFR from coronary CT angiography**.
Per the FDA summary it combines coronary anatomy with **plaque composition** ('BioIntegrated'); the predicate uses computational fluid dynamics. 'Most accurate FFR-CT' is Elucid's own claim.

**FDA indication**: software for **clinically stable patients with suspected CAD** (the device description says known or suspected), to **support functional evaluation** of CAD. Elucid's 'who needs invasive angiography' framing is not in the indication.
Validation **ELUCIDATE** (NCT06018194): **retrospective, multicentre (11 sites), 347 patients, 491 vessels**, against **invasive FFR**.
Per vessel (FDA 510(k) summary): **sensitivity 92.2%**, **specificity 93.1%**, unadjusted **PPV 84.4%**, **NPV 96.7%**. US cohort (n=257 vessels): **90.9% / 89.2%**.

The **US retrospective cohort** was enriched for borderline disease (FFR 0.75-0.85) because only paired CCTA and invasive FFR were usable; prospectively collected data from an outside-US site added non-ischaemic vessels to the overall cohort.
Caveats: **retrospective** validation at 11 sites (9 US, 2 outside US); figures come from the FDA summary and company release; no peer-reviewed paper found.
